overall_diagnosis: The task’s failures center on a contract mismatch between the documented segment normalization/merge requirements and what the pipeline (video-processor) expects, compounded by an implementation gap in the segment combiner. segment-combiner currently only concatenates/sorts and trusts input durations, while the docs (also truncated) imply a fully normalized, merged, non-overlapping removal list. video-processor’s pipeline/checks reference this “normalized merged removal-segments JSON” but are truncated/underspecified, so downstream processing and report math can become inconsistent when overlaps/adjacency or invalid segments exist.

diagnosed_skills.diagnosis: Implementation does not perform the documented normalization: no validation/clamping, no overlap/adjacency merging, and it sums provided durations instead of recomputing from start/end. This can yield overlapping/invalid removal intervals and incorrect total_duration_seconds, breaking downstream removal correctness and report consistency.
diagnosed_skills.repair_instruction: Implement full normalization and merging: robustly parse segments from inputs, coerce start/end to numeric, clamp start/end to >=0 (and optionally clamp end to a provided/known total duration), drop/repair segments where end <= start, sort by start, merge overlapping or directly-adjacent segments using the explicit rule next.start <= prev.end, recompute each segment.duration = end - start, and compute total_segments and total_duration_seconds from the merged output. If duration clamping is needed, add an optional CLI parameter (e.g., --total-duration) while maintaining backward compatibility.

diagnosed_skills.diagnosis: The normalization/merge contract is truncated/incomplete and may be ambiguous about endpoint semantics and adjacency merging. This ambiguity propagates to downstream tools and evaluation (e.g., whether [start,end] vs [start,end) is used, and how to treat adjacent intervals).
diagnosed_skills.repair_instruction: Complete and tighten the spec: explicitly define segment schema (numeric start/end in seconds) and endpoint convention (recommend half-open [start,end) to avoid off-by-one ambiguity); define exact merge condition (merge when next.start <= prev.end, including adjacency); require validation (numeric), clamping to non-negative timeline and (if total duration known/provided) end <= total_duration; specify handling of invalid segments (drop/repair end<=start); require sorting, merging, and recomputation of duration and aggregate totals from merged results. Ensure “Output guarantees” is not truncated and matches the script output keys.

diagnosed_skills.diagnosis: Pipeline guidance and completion checks are truncated/underspecified relative to the segment-combiner contract, so it may not clearly enforce consuming the combiner’s normalized merged output and validating segment correctness before processing and reporting.
diagnosed_skills.repair_instruction: Align the end-to-end pipeline and checks with the repaired segment-combiner contract: explicitly require using the combiner’s normalized merged segments JSON as the sole removal input; document expected keys and segment semantics consistent with the combiner (including adjacency rule and endpoint convention); add explicit preflight validations (sorted, non-overlapping after merge, clamped within duration, end>start, durations recomputed); ensure the report generator uses the same merged segments so segments_removed matches actual removals; tighten completion checks to confirm artifact existence and basic math consistency (original_duration ≈ compressed_duration + removed_duration) without contradictory requirements.
